podcast.body: Valens' debut record, which featured a foundational one-four-five-one chord progression common in many Latin songs. The recording involved session musicians Red Callender on bass, Earl Palmer on drums, and Ernie Freeman on piano, with guitarists occasionally contributing a tic-tac bass (a six-string bass guitar known for its unique tone, characteristic of many LA records). Many of these musicians later formed parts of The Wrecking Crew. It achieved minor chart success, peaking at number 42. Valens demonstrated his spontaneous performing style by significantly varying the lyrics and melody in live performances compared to the studio version. "Come on, let's go! Was a minor hit, reaching number 42 under heart 100."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
